summary: Qatar grants free visa waivers on arrival to citizens of over 100 countries — 90 days within 180 for EU and Schengen-area passports, 30 extendable days for most others including the US, UK and much of Asia and Latin America — and routes remaining nationalities through the official Hayya platform for a tourist visa.

conditionalWaivers.text: GCC residents in approved professions (and their accompanying family) can obtain a visa on arrival in Qatar — confirm eligibility on the official Hayya portal.

source.name: Qatar MOFA — visa waiver and entry information

fee.notes: Approximate — the exact fee is shown during the Hayya application; confirmed accommodation in Qatar is required.

source.name: Hayya — official Qatar entry and visa platform

passportValidity.text: Your passport should be valid for at least 6 months on arrival. Some sources state that 3 months' validity is accepted for certain visa-waiver nationalities — carry 6 months to be safe.

source.name: Ministry of Foreign Affairs of Qatar
Ministry of Foreign Affairs of Qatar

travelInsurance.text: No insurance is checked for short visa-waiver visits, but visitors staying longer than 30 days and most visa applicants must hold health insurance from a Qatari-approved insurer under the mandatory visitor health insurance scheme.

source.name: Ministry of Foreign Affairs of Qatar

onwardTicket.text: Visa-waiver visitors should hold a confirmed onward or return ticket; airlines and border officers may also ask for proof of accommodation.

source.name: Ministry of Foreign Affairs of Qatar

proofOfFunds.text: No fixed amount is published; border officers may ask visitors to show sufficient means for their stay.

source.name: Ministry of Foreign Affairs of Qatar

currencyLimits.text: Cash, cheques or precious metals worth QAR 50,000 or more (or the foreign-currency equivalent) must be declared on arrival and departure.

source.name: Ministry of Foreign Affairs of Qatar

notes: Alcohol may not be brought into Qatar, including duty-free purchases made en route — it is confiscated at the border.
Narcotics, pork products and pornographic material are prohibited; many medications require a prescription — check before travelling.
E-cigarettes and vaping products are restricted — bringing them in can lead to confiscation and fines.

payments.text: Cards and contactless payments are accepted almost everywhere, from malls to taxis and the Doha Metro. Cash is only occasionally useful at Souq Waqif stalls and for small tips.

safety.text: Qatar has very low crime and is one of the safest countries for travellers. The main considerations are legal and cultural: strict rules on alcohol, drugs, public behaviour and photography of sensitive sites.

source.name: U.S. Department of State — Qatar Travel Advisory

bestTimeToVisit.text: November to March offers warm, pleasant weather for the Corniche, desert trips and outdoor souqs; summer is extremely hot and humid.

idp.text: Qatar is a party to the 1968 Vienna Convention on Road Traffic but not to the 1949 Geneva one, so the International Driving Permit it is bound to recognise is the 1968 Vienna version. A permit issued under the 1949 Geneva Convention carries no treaty obligation here.

source.name: UN Treaty Collection — Convention on Road Traffic (Vienna, 1968), status of parties
source.instrument: Convention on Road Traffic, Vienna, 8 November 1968 (UNTS vol. 1042, p. 17)

driving.text: Qatar is a party to the 1968 Vienna Convention on Road Traffic but not to the 1949 Geneva one, so the International Driving Permit it is bound to recognise is the 1968 Vienna version. A permit issued under the 1949 Geneva Convention carries no treaty obligation here. Whether a permit is required in addition to a national licence, and for how long a foreign licence may be used, are set by national road law and have not been checked for Qatar yet.

source.name: UN Treaty Collection — Convention on Road Traffic (Vienna, 1968), status of parties
source.instrument: Convention on Road Traffic, Vienna, 8 November 1968 (UNTS vol. 1042, p. 17)

tips.text: From June to September temperatures routinely exceed 45°C with high humidity — plan outdoor activities for early morning or after dark, and stay hydrated.
Alcohol is legal only in licensed hotel bars and restaurants — never drink in public or drive after drinking (zero tolerance), and do not bring alcohol into the country, even duty-free.
Dress modestly in public places — shoulders and knees covered is the safe rule at malls, souqs and government buildings; swimwear is fine at hotel pools and beaches.
The official Hayya app and portal (hayya.qa) is the single place to check visa eligibility, apply for a tourist visa and manage entry — avoid third-party visa websites.

faq.question: Do US citizens need a visa for Qatar?
faq.answer: No advance visa is needed. US passport holders receive a free visa waiver on arrival valid for 30 days, which can be extended once for a further 30 days from inside Qatar.

faq.question: How long can EU citizens stay in Qatar?
faq.answer: Citizens of EU and Schengen-area countries (plus Switzerland) get a free waiver on arrival allowing up to 90 days within any 180-day period — the most generous tier of Qatar's waiver scheme.

faq.question: What is Hayya and do I need it to enter Qatar?
faq.answer: Hayya (hayya.qa) is Qatar's official entry and visa platform, kept on after the 2022 World Cup. Visa-waiver nationalities can simply arrive with their passport, while nationalities that need a visa apply for the Hayya A1 tourist visa there — roughly QAR 100, with confirmed accommodation required.

faq.question: Can tourists drink alcohol in Qatar?
faq.answer: Yes, but only in licensed venues — mainly hotel bars and restaurants. Drinking in public is illegal, there is zero tolerance for drink-driving, and you cannot bring alcohol into the country even from duty-free.

faq.question: Can I extend my visa-free stay in Qatar?
faq.answer: Visitors on the 30-day waiver can extend once for a further 30 days online or through the Ministry of Interior before the first period expires. The 90-in-180-day waiver for EU passports is not extendable beyond its limit.
